newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot gas rises at exports after NYMEX rally.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas rises at exports after NYMEX rally.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices held in Alberta but scored gains at the export points, market sources said Tuesday.

Spot prices at the AECO storage hub in Alberta eased by about one cent to C$1.45-1.46 per gigajoule. September AECO was talked equally lower at C$1.41 in thin trade, while October prices were quoted at C$1.51-1.515. One-year business hovered around C$1.72, traders said.
Temperatures in Calgary were forecast to still reach highs in the low-to-mid 70 (degrees F) this week, according to Weather Services Corp.

Petro-Canada's Hanlan-Robb gas plant west of Edmonton in Alberta was expected to reach full power by Wednesday or Thursday, the company said. The unit was taken off line last Wednesday for a scheduled turnaround, affecting about 200 million cubic feet per day of gas.
At Sumas, Wash., spot gas prices rose two cents to about $1.09-1.12 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) as Northwest utilities continued to demand substantial volumes of gas.

In the East, Niagara prices followed futures higher to the mid-$2.60s after NYMEX's September contract reached a new high of $2.605 late Monday. A correction on NYMEX today will likely lead to softer prices at the export point on Wednesday, traders said.
